questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A petroleum fraction having boiling range $\text{70} - {\text{200}^{o} \text{C}$ and containing $\text{6} - \text{10}$ carbon atoms per molecule is called
questions.solution:
The bulk of a typical gasoline consists of hydrocarbons with between $4$ and $12$ carbon atoms per molecule (commonly referred to as $\text{C4} - \text{C12}$). It is a mixture of paraffins (alkanes), cycloalkanes (naphthenes), and olefins (alkenes), where the usage of the terms paraffin and olefin is particular to the oil industry. The actual ratio depends on:

  • The oil refinery that makes the gasoline, as not all refineries have the same set of processing units;
  • The crude oil feed used by the refinery;
  • The grade of gasoline, in particular, the octane rating.

Below carbon atoms per molecule are mentioned.

(i) Gasoline ${C}_{6} - {C}_{10}$

(ii) Kerosene ${C}_{10} - {C}_{13}$

(iii) Gas oil ${C}_{13} - {C}_{18}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: ${\text{SO}_{2}$ is considered as an air pollutant because
options: Its concentration increases with temperature increase of atmosphere.
It is used as an insecticide which is air pollutant
It reacts with ${O}_{2}$ and ${H}_{2} \text{O}$ to produce acid rain
It is a strong oxidant and oxidizes other components of atmosphere
questions.solution: ${\text{SO}_{2}$ is considered as air pollutant because it reacts with ${O}_{2}$ and ${H}_{2} \text{O}$ to produce acid rain. Oxides from nitrogen and sulphur, released into the atmosphere from thermal power plants, industries and automobiles are the main sources of acid rain. These oxides on oxidation followed by hydrolysis give sulphuric acid and nitric acid that get dissolved in rain water and are responsible for the acidity of rain.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the pollutant gases largely responsible for the discoloured and lustreless nature of marble of the Taj Mahal.
questions.solution:
Industries present nearby Taj Mahal produce a lot of $N{O}_{2}$ and $S{O}_{2}$ gases which react with water, oxygen and other chemicals to form sulphuric acid and nitric acid. These then mix with water and make the rain acidic which than react with marble to decolourise it as follows
$CaC{O}_{3} + {H}_{2}S{O}_{4} \to CaS{O}_{4} + C{O}_{2} + {H}_{2}O$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A water sample has ppm level concentration of following anions, $F^{-} = 10; S{O}_{4}^{2 -} = 100; N{O}_{3}^{-} = 50$. The anion/anions that make/makes the water sample unsuitable for drinking is/are
questions.solution:
Above 500 ppm of $S{O}_{4}^{2 -}$ ions in drinking water, can cause laxative effect otherwise lesser ppm value is permissible for drinking.

Maximum limit of $N{O}_{3}^{-}$ ions in drinking water is 50 ppm, above this limit it can cause the disease like methemoglobinemia.

More than 1 ppm $F^{-}$ ions in drinking water are not fit for drinking, it can cause decay of bones and teeth.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Photochemical smog consists of excessive amount of X, in addition to aldehydes, ketones, peroxyacetyl nitrates (PAN) and so forth X is
questions.solution:
Chemical pollutants in photochemical smog are nitrogen oxides (NO and $N{O}_{2}$ ), volatile organic compounds, ozone $\left({O}_{3}\right)$ , peroxyacetyl nitrates.

In the presence of sunlight of the following reactions take place

$N{O}_{2}\overset{hv}{→}NO + O$

$O + {O}_{2} \to {O}_{3}$

${O}_{3} + NO \to N{O}_{2} + {O}_{2}$

Hence, it consists of excessive amount of ozone melecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following are common components of photochemical smog?
$1.$ Chlorofluorocarbons
$2.$ Acrolein
$3.$ Ozone
$4.$ Peroxyacetyl nitrate
questions.solution:
The common components of photochemical smog are Ozone, Nitric oxide, Acrolein, Formaldehyde
and Peroxyacehyl nitrate (PAN).
Hence Chlorofluorocarbons (CFC) is not common component of photochemical smog.
